answers.rationale: FR2 and SR2 require a hand-written parser that reads bytes directly (not a wrapper around hyper/httparse). answers.rationale: SR3 explicitly requires a trie with literal, parameter, and wildcard segment types; lookup must be O(path-length) and must not allocate per request beyond the parameter map.

answers.rationale: FR3 requires explicit method dispatch; HEAD falls back to GET with body suppressed and OPTIONS auto-lists methods. There is no mention of GET automatically registering POST — that would be inconsistent with explicit method dispatch.

presented_options.D: logger, gzip, token-bucket rate limit per client IP, CORS, double-submit-cookie CSRF, basic auth

answers.rationale: FR5 lists exactly: logger, gzip, rate limiting (token bucket per client IP), CORS, CSRF (double-submit cookie), and basic auth. Option C replaces rate limit with sliding-window per API key, CSRF with OAuth2 bearer, and omits basic auth — inconsistent with the spec.

presented_options.A: exits with code 1 because at least one request was still in flight when the timeout elapsed
presented_options.B: waits indefinitely until every in-flight request completes, then exits with code 0

presented_options.D: aborts immediately on SIGTERM, replying 503 to all in-flight connections, then exits non-zero

answers.rationale: FR10 specifies graceful_timeout_s with default 30s. SIGTERM arrives, server stops accepting new connections and waits up to 30s. The two handlers needing 60s exceed the timeout and are abandoned. Process exits with code 0 per spec.

answers.rationale: SR2 explicitly forbids the HTTP parser from depending on the router module. The parser must be isolated for fuzz-testing; importing router types (trie node types or route-match results) would violate this requirement.
